title: BCL2, Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma, Burkitt Starry Sky, and Mantle Cell Lymphoma

steps.tx: The proto-oncogene **BCL2 protein** functions as a vital mitochondrial gatekeeper that suppresses programmed cell death. Located on the outer mitochondrial membrane, BCL2 binds and neutralizes pro-apoptotic multidomain effectors BAX and BAK, preventing mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization and blocking the release of cytochrome c into the cytosol. In follicular lymphoma, the chromosomal translocation t(14;18)(q32;q21) juxtaposes BCL2 with the immunoglobulin heavy-chain locus enhancer, causing constitutive overexpression of BCL2 that renders germinal centre B-cells resistant to physiological apoptosis.
steps.say: The BCL2 proto-oncogene encodes a critical mitochondrial membrane protein that blocks apoptosis. By binding and neutralizing pro-apoptotic effectors like BAX and BAK, BCL2 preserves mitochondrial integrity and halts the release of cytochrome c. When the t(14;18) translocation moves BCL2 under the control of the immunoglobulin heavy chain promoter, germinal center B-cells overexpress BCL2 and acquire an unnatural survival advantage, driving follicular lymphoma.

right.title: Pro-Apoptotic Effectors
points: Includes BAX, BAK, BIM, and PUMA
Form pore complexes in outer membrane
Release cytochrome c to activate caspase 9

steps.tx: Representing thirty to forty percent of adult non-Hodgkin lymphomas, **diffuse large B-cell lymphoma** is the most common aggressive lymphoid malignancy worldwide. Histological sections reveal diffuse sheets of large, atypical neoplastic lymphoid cells that completely efface normal lymph node architecture, displaying vesicular nuclei, prominent nucleoli, and abundant basophilic cytoplasm. Clinically, patients present with rapidly enlarging nodal masses or symptomatic extranodal disease, most frequently involving the stomach, ileocecal region, central nervous system, Waldeyer ring, or bone.
steps.say: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma is the most common non-Hodgkin lymphoma in adults, accounting for more than thirty percent of cases. Microscopic sections show total architectural obliteration by diffuse sheets of large malignant B-cells with vesicular chromatin and prominent nucleoli. Patients present with rapidly enlarging lymph nodes or aggressive extranodal masses in the gastrointestinal tract, brain, or Waldeyer ring, requiring prompt diagnostic biopsy and immediate treatment.

rows: Young females with bulky anterior mass

steps.tx: The therapeutic cornerstone for diffuse large B-cell lymphoma is **R-CHOP immunochemotherapy**, combining the anti-CD20 chimeric monoclonal antibody rituximab with cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, and prednisolone. Rituximab binds surface CD20, triggering complement-dependent cytotoxicity, antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity, and direct apoptosis of neoplastic B-cells. Administered every twenty-one days for six cycles, this regimen achieves durable cures in over sixty-five percent of patients. Interim positron emission tomography after three to four cycles assesses early metabolic response and guides potential treatment consolidation.
steps.say: Standard frontline therapy for diffuse large B-cell lymphoma is the R-CHOP regimen, which pairs the anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody rituximab with cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, and oral prednisone. Rituximab tags malignant B-cells for destruction by natural killer cells and complement. Administering six cycles of R-CHOP cures roughly two-thirds of patients. Mid-treatment FDG-PET imaging verifies metabolic response and separates responsive tumors from refractory clones.

steps.tx: Burkitt lymphoma is an extraordinarily aggressive B-cell neoplasm boasting the fastest doubling time of any human malignancy, with a cellular proliferation fraction (Ki-67 index) approaching one hundred percent. Histopathological examination demonstrates a classic **starry-sky appearance** produced by a monotonous background sea of intermediate-sized, basophilic neoplastic lymphoid cells interspersed with numerous pale, benign tingible-body macrophages. These active histiocytes ingest abundant apoptotic nuclear debris resulting from the astronomical cell turnover and spontaneous programmed cell death inherent to the tumour.
steps.say: Burkitt lymphoma has the shortest doubling time of any human cancer, doubling in volume every twenty-four hours with a Ki-67 proliferation index near one hundred percent. Microscopic inspection demonstrates the pathognomonic starry-sky pattern: dark, uniform basophilic lymphoblasts form a deep blue night sky, while scattered pale tingible-body macrophages packed with swallowed apoptotic nuclear debris shine like bright stars across the tissue.

vis.alt: Micrograph of Burkitt lymphoma showing starry-sky pattern with tingible body macrophages
vis.caption: Burkitt lymphoma with starry sky histology and jaw or abdominal presentation.

steps.tx: Pathogenesis in Burkitt lymphoma centers on the reciprocal **translocation t(8;14)(q24;q32)**, identified in eighty-five percent of cases, or variant translocations t(2;8) and t(8;22). These translocations relocate the c-MYC proto-oncogene from chromosome 8 into juxtaposition with the transcriptionally hyperactive immunoglobulin heavy-chain (IGH) locus on chromosome 14, or light-chain loci. Constitutive overexpression of the MYC transcription factor drives relentless cell cycle progression through G1/S, activates aerobic glycolysis, and accelerates cellular growth while rendering cells exquisitely sensitive to metabolic stress.
steps.say: Burkitt lymphoma is driven by translocations involving the MYC proto-oncogene on chromosome eight, most commonly the reciprocal translocation t(8;14) involving the immunoglobulin heavy chain locus. Juxtaposition with the powerful immunoglobulin enhancer causes constant, dysregulated overexpression of the MYC transcription factor. MYC forces resting cells through the cell cycle, promotes aerobic glycolysis, and produces relentless, explosive clonal expansion.

steps.tx: Mantle cell lymphoma is an incurable, aggressive B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma arising from naïve B-cells within the mantle zones of lymphoid follicles. Neoplastic cells harbor the pathognomonic chromosomal **translocation t(11;14)(q13;q32)**, which translocates the CCND1 gene on chromosome 11 to the immunoglobulin heavy-chain locus on chromosome 14. This rearrangement causes marked overexpression of cyclin D1, which associates with cyclin-dependent kinase 4 to phosphorylate retinoblastoma protein. Neoplastic cells characteristically express CD5, CD19, and SOX11, but lack CD23 expression.
steps.say: Mantle cell lymphoma arises from mature B-cells occupying the follicular mantle zone. It is genetically defined by the reciprocal translocation t(11;14), which brings the cyclin D1 gene under the influence of the immunoglobulin heavy chain promoter. Overexpressed cyclin D1 drives uncontrolled G1-to-S cell cycle transition. Flow cytometry reveals a characteristic profile: cells co-express B-cell markers with CD5 and nuclear SOX11, but test negative for CD23, clearly separating them from CLL.

vis.caption: Mantle cell lymphoma manifestations including lymphomatous polyposis and nodal disease.

steps.tx: Because aggressive lymphomas like Burkitt and high-burden diffuse large B-cell lymphoma exhibit extreme cell turnover and chemotherapy sensitivity, initiating systemic cytotoxic treatment risks catastrophic **acute tumour lysis syndrome**. Massive intracellular lysis discharges vast quantities of potassium, phosphate, and nucleic acids into the systemic circulation. Catabolism of nucleic acids generates insoluble uric acid crystals that obstruct renal collecting tubules, while hyperphosphataemia precipitates calcium phosphate in renal parenchyma, producing life-threatening hyperkalaemia, severe hypocalcaemia, acute renal failure, and fatal cardiac arrhythmias.
steps.say: Tumour lysis syndrome is a medical emergency triggered by the rapid destruction of malignant cells following initiation of chemotherapy. Lysis floods the blood with potassium, phosphate, and nucleic acids. Uric acid crystals precipitate inside renal tubules while hyperphosphataemia drives metastatic calcium phosphate deposition, causing acute kidney injury, severe hypocalcaemic tetany, and lethal ventricular arrhythmias. Prophylaxis with aggressive hydration and rasburicase is mandatory prior to treatment.

rows: Catabolism of cellular purine nucleic acids
Tetany, carpopedal spasm, seizures, long QTc

steps.tx: Risk stratification and clinical trial design in aggressive non-Hodgkin lymphomas utilize the **International Prognostic Index**, which quantifies patient survival based on five independent baseline adverse parameters. The scoring system assigns one point for age greater than sixty years, Ann Arbor Stage III or IV disease, elevated serum lactate dehydrogenase above normal limits, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 2 or higher, and involvement of more than one extranodal site. Low-risk patients score 0 to 1, while high-risk patients score 4 to 5.
steps.say: The International Prognostic Index predicts outcome in patients with aggressive lymphomas such as diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. Clinicians evaluate five simple clinical variables: age over sixty, stage three or four disease, elevated serum lactate dehydrogenase, poor performance status, and more than one extranodal disease site. Patients with zero or one factor achieve excellent five-year survival, while those with four or five risk factors require consideration of intensified regimens.

points: Stage I or II localized disease

right.title: High-Risk IPI (4-5 Points)

quiz.q: Which chromosomal translocation drives the pathogenesis of Burkitt lymphoma by juxtaposing c-MYC with the immunoglobulin heavy-chain locus?
quiz.explain: The reciprocal translocation t(8;14)(q24;q32) moves the c-MYC oncogene on chromosome 8 under the control of the IGH enhancer on chromosome 14, driving Burkitt lymphoma.

quiz.q: Which immunophenotypic marker combination distinguishes mantle cell lymphoma from chronic lymphocytic leukaemia?
options: CD5 positive, Cyclin D1 positive, CD23 negative
CD5 positive, CD23 positive, Cyclin D1 negative
CD10 positive, BCL2 positive, CD5 negative
CD103 positive, CD25 positive, CD11c positive
quiz.explain: Mantle cell lymphoma co-expresses CD5 and Cyclin D1 but is CD23 negative, whereas CLL is CD5 positive and CD23 positive but Cyclin D1 negative.

quiz.q: What is the primary mechanism by which BCL2 protein prevents cellular apoptosis in follicular lymphoma?
options: Inhibits BAX and BAK to block mitochondrial cytochrome c release
Activates executioner caspase 3 and caspase 7 directly
Promotes Fas death receptor trimerization on the cell membrane
Phosphorylates and degrades the p53 tumor suppressor protein
quiz.explain: BCL2 is an anti-apoptotic protein that sequesters pro-apoptotic BAX and BAK, maintaining mitochondrial outer membrane integrity and preventing cytochrome c release.
